text:
maria: quick thought — our current pruning strategy (time-based + reference-count) trips in air-gapped installs when operators hold activation ledgers for long grace windows. we should discuss a design that avoids deleting artifacts an operator may still need to roll back to.
jon: today most operators keep a 7d acceptance window. but some customers want 30d. pruning based solely on 'last-referenced' will delete bundles that are still 'accepted' but not actively referenced. :thinking: 
kevin: idea: introduce a lightweight operator heartbeat record in the control-manifest that's replicated into the offline index. prune only after heartbeat TTL + tombstone grace. heartbeat is ~small metadata entry, not the full blob.
carmen: sounds promising. edge case: what if the operator crashes and the heartbeat never gets refreshed? we might retain huge blobs unnecessarily. we need a hard cap and an emergency reclaim policy.
maria: agreed — propose two tiers: 1) soft-retain = heartbeat TTL (configurable), 2) hard-cap = absolute retention (e.g., 90d). if disk pressure, reclamation uses LRU across soft-retain items but never reclaims items flagged as active in the last X days unless operator explicitly marks 'evictable'.
jon: operator UX: expose a CLI to mark acceptance windows per component and to force-evict. e.g. `rctl operator set-retain --component=modelstore --days=60` and `rctl operator evict --component=foo --force`. small sample manifest addition:
```yaml
metadata:
  operator-heartbeat: true
  retention-days: 30
```
kevin: implementation notes: the heartbeat should be compact, signed by operator key, and include a monotonic epoch so we can distinguish stale heartbeats from clock skew. storage engine keeps a small index mapping artifact->heartbeatEpoch. PR will add a compact RPC for operators to push heartbeat during reconcile loops.
ops: concern: backups/restore. if operator heartbeat is lost during restore, we'd retain nothing and potentially prune needed artifacts. suggestion: when restoring, mark all artifacts referenced by last-known activation ledger as preserved for a temporary restore-grace period (configurable).
carmen: another tradeoff: some customers run air-gapped with very low disk. we should allow operator to tier artifacts: keep metadata-only thin-client (ability to stream on-demand from a seeded cache) vs full local copy. can we support on-demand fetch for large model shards?
maria: yes but that's more like partial-shard activation which adds runtime complexity. for now let's scope: heartbeat+soft/hard windows + operator CLI + restore-grace. followup RFC should cover partial-shard streaming.
jon: +1. anyone opposed to making soft-retain default 30d and hard-cap 90d? customers can override.
kevin: fine. i'll draft a follow-up RFC sketch with sequence diagrams and the new RPC endpoints. will call it "operator-heartbeat-retention".
maria: thanks — small ask: include compatibility note for older operators that don't emit heartbeat (treat them as legacy and use last-referenced time only). add a migration plan to backfill acceptance ledgers where possible.
deploy-bot: deploy status: no runtime changes required for hosted. will target dedicated/private v0.13.0 for operator heartbeat API. :white_check_mark:
ops: I'll add a runbook snippet for restore scenarios and emergency evict.
maria: great. closing action items: kevin write RFC, jon add CLI UX, ops write restore runbook. anyone want to add anything else? :thumbsup:
